S1 disabled (engine=strategy2.py). 2026-08-26 session: NO PARAMETER CHANGES. Two findings -- one measured for the first time, one that killed a recommendation.

1. RATCHET SLIPPAGE -- new, and it is a first-order leak. locked_r is the R level update_sl() moves the stop to; rr is what the trade realised. They should be EQUAL -- that is the whole promise of a ratchet, an invariant rather than a statistic. Nothing had ever compared them. Over the 3 armed trades that recorded a lock: SOL +2.50 -> +2.476 (leak 1.0%), SUI +2.50 -> +2.441 (2.4%), ETH +2.50 -> +2.169 (13.2%). Total leak 0.414R of 7.50R locked. Book sumR is +2.61, so without the leak it would be +3.02 -- slippage is 14% of gross. Four earlier armed trades predate locked_r and are named as a coverage gap rather than dropped; one of them, AVAX 2026-08-11, is confirmed by bot.log to have locked +3R and delivered +2.632R, a further 0.368R. Counting it, the leak is ~0.78R against a +2.61R book: roughly 23% of gross.

MECHANISM. The ratchet arms the moment price reaches TRAIL_START_R, so the new stop is placed at the price that just traded -- essentially AT market. One adverse tick fires it into an IOC. ETH 2026-08-25 armed at 09:52:57 and filled 24s later 1.05% beyond its trigger. This is not new behaviour; it is the same at-market placement seen on BTC 2026-08-03 (armed +0.75R, filled +0.706R 22s later). What is new is that it is measured every night now instead of noticed anecdotally. Added as a permanent RATCHET SLIPPAGE section in analyze.full_report.

EXECUTOR FINDING (reported, values unchanged). The two stop-placement sites used slippage caps differing 6.7x, both as bare local variables in different functions, which is why nobody had ever compared them: place bracket 0.003, update_sl 0.02. The LOOSER cap guards the ratchet stop -- the order protecting 100% of this strategy's realised edge. ETH's 1.05% adverse fill sat comfortably inside 2% and was therefore accepted in full; under 0.3% it would have been capped at roughly +2.40R instead of +2.17R. Lifted both to named module constants BRACKET_SLIP_CAP / RATCHET_SLIP_CAP with the trade-off documented. VALUES UNCHANGED -- narrowing RATCHET_SLIP_CAP is a deployed exit-behaviour change with a real tail risk: a Hyperliquid trigger with isMarket:True fires an IOC, and the unfilled remainder is CANCELLED rather than rested, so too tight a cap can leave a ratcheted position with nothing resting against it. Kamran's call.

2. THE ENTRY BANDS WERE A FALSE LEAD, AND IT IS NOW SETTLED. For four sessions running the ENTRY CONDITION BANDS table has implied tightening the gate (ADX 15-20 n=3 meanR +1.485 vs 20-25 n=14 -0.132; stretch 3+ n=11 +0.603 vs 2-3 n=5 -0.609). Tested with portfolio2 -- the instrument that is VALID for entry-side questions -- on 20 coins, 5000 1h bars, live exit params. Rejected in both directions, monotonically. net% / ex-top5%: MAX_ADX 25(live) +49.18/+25.67, 22 +17.92/-0.19, 20 +6.04/-9.26, 18 +2.32/-6.38. stretch 1.5(live) +49.18/+25.67, 2.5 +38.99/+15.97, 3.0 +29.38/+8.54, 3.5 +16.21/-4.63.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ex-top5, NOT net. Every tightened gate still posts a positive net while its ex-top5 -- the edge with its five best trades deleted -- is NEGATIVE. The live gate is the only setting tested whose edge survives losing its tail. The bands disagree because they slice n<20 post-hoc and are conditioned on exactly the tail ex-top5 removes: 'ADX 15-20 WR 100%' is three trades; the same cell at n=23 in the sweep has ex-top5 -9.26%. The bands section now carries this counter-result inline so a fifth session does not re-derive the same false lead. Second night running that a sweep overruled an anecdote, which is the point of running it.
